mcq.q: What is the primary goal of software engineering?
o: Writing code as fast as possible
Building software that meets user requirements within budget and schedule
mcq.e: Software engineering is a disciplined approach; coding fast is only a small part of it.

mcq.q: Which is the correct order of the SDLC phases?
o: Analysis, Design, Coding, Testing, Operation & Maintenance
mcq.e: Analysis always comes before Design, and Testing always comes before Maintenance.

mcq.q: A feasibility study is carried out to decide:
o: Whether the project should be built at all
How many test cases are needed
mcq.e: It is done before the project starts and checks technology, finance, time and resources.

mcq.q: Project size is judged under which type of feasibility?
mcq.e: Project size falls under technical feasibility; cost-benefit analysis is economic feasibility.

mcq.q: The activity that identifies, controls, audits and reports modifications made to software is:
mcq.e: SCM keeps all versions consistent by tracking every modification.

mcq.q: Recovering the design and requirements of old software by studying its code is called:
mcq.e: Reverse engineering only understands the system; re-engineering goes further and rebuilds it.

mcq.q: Which model is called the Linear Sequential Model and was given by Royce?
mcq.e: The Waterfall model is the oldest paradigm, with each phase completed before the next begins.

mcq.q: The basic assumption of the Waterfall model is that:
o: Requirements are frozen before design begins
Risk is analysed in every loop
mcq.e: Because requirements are frozen, linear models are incompatible with changing requirements.

mcq.q: Which model is best when the customer is not sure what he wants and requirements keep changing?
mcq.e: Users react to a concrete working model, which clarifies the requirements.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a phase of the Prototype model?
mcq.e: The real product is engineered only at the end; full coding is not a separate prototyping phase.

mcq.q: The two flavours of evolutionary development are:
mcq.e: Evolutionary development builds the system through successive versions in these two ways.

mcq.q: The Incremental model is a combination of:
mcq.e: Each increment is built linearly, while the series of increments behaves like prototyping.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a phase of the RAD model?
mcq.e: RAD phases are business, data, process modelling, application generation and testing.

mcq.q: RAD is NOT suitable when:
mcq.e: RAD relies on quickly assembling well-understood reusable components, so high technical risk is a problem.

mcq.q: The Spiral model was given by:
mcq.e: Barry Boehm proposed the Spiral model in 1986.

mcq.q: The most important feature of the Spiral model is:
mcq.e: It is the only model giving explicit recognition of risk on every cycle.

mcq.q: Why is the Spiral model called the meta model?
o: Other models like waterfall and prototyping can fit inside its loops
It was the first model invented
mcq.e: Different process models can be accommodated within the loops of the spiral.

mcq.q: Which of the following is a four-activity loop of the Spiral model?
o: Planning, risk analysis, engineering, customer evaluation
mcq.e: Every spiral loop contains planning, risk analysis, engineering and customer evaluation.

mcq.q: Which is the correct order of Pressman's five generic framework activities?
mcq.e: The order is Communication, Planning, Modelling, Construction, Deployment.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid software life-cycle model?
mcq.e: Valid models include Waterfall, Iterative, Prototype, Incremental, RAD, Spiral, Agile, JAD and V-Model; 'Circular' is not one.

mcq.q: In the V-Model, design is matched with which testing phase?
mcq.e: Requirements pair with acceptance testing, design with integration testing and coding with unit testing.

mcq.q: In the MVC architecture, the component that handles user input and connects the other two is the:
mcq.e: Model keeps the data, View displays it, and Controller handles input.

mcq.q: Which model shows how software responds to external events, using state diagrams?
mcq.e: The behaviour model covers response to events; context model shows boundaries and data model shows information.

mcq.q: Which is the correct order of requirements engineering activities?
o: Feasibility study, elicitation and analysis, specification, validation
mcq.e: The four activities run in the order feasibility, elicitation & analysis, specification, validation.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT contained in an SRS?
mcq.e: The SRS is a black-box specification; algorithms belong to the design phase.

mcq.q: Maintainability, portability and robustness are examples of which requirements?
mcq.e: They describe how well the system works, so they are non-functional requirements.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a recognised sub-type of non-functional requirements?
mcq.e: The sub-types are product, organisational and external.

mcq.q: The group elicitation technique in which stakeholders throw ideas freely is:
mcq.e: Brainstorming is the group technique of free idea generation.

mcq.q: In a DFD, the Level-0 diagram is also called the:
mcq.e: It draws the whole system as a single bubble with its external entities.

mcq.q: In a DFD, two parallel lines (open rectangle) represent a:
mcq.e: A data store is data at rest; a process is a circle, a flow is an arrow and an external entity is a rectangle.

mcq.q: Which statement about UML is correct?
o: It is a software process model
It is the standard notation for object-oriented design
It is a programming language compiler
mcq.e: UML is a notation, not a process.

mcq.q: Which is NOT an element of the requirements model?
mcq.e: The elements are scenario-based, class-based, behavioural and flow-oriented; 'usage-based' is not one.

mcq.q: Cohesion refers to:
o: Functional strength of a single module
Number of modules in a system
Size of the program in KLOC
mcq.e: Cohesion measures how strongly elements inside one module belong together; interdependence between modules is coupling.

mcq.q: Which is the best (strongest) type of cohesion?
mcq.e: Functional cohesion, where all elements achieve one single function, is the ideal.

mcq.q: A module whose elements perform a similar category of operations, such as all error handling or all data input, has which cohesion?
mcq.e: Logical cohesion groups elements by similar category of operation.

mcq.q: Which is the worst type of coupling?
mcq.e: Content coupling, where one module uses code or data inside another, is the worst.

mcq.q: Modules sharing the same global data area exhibit which coupling?
mcq.e: Common coupling means a shared global data area.

mcq.q: Which software architecture style is exemplified by the Unix pipeline?
mcq.e: Each filter performs one transformation and passes data through a pipe to the next.

mcq.q: Verification answers the question:
o: Are we building the right product?
Are we building the product right?
mcq.e: Verification checks work against the specification; validation asks whether it is the right product.

mcq.q: Which is the correct order of testing levels?
mcq.e: The four levels are always performed unit, integration, system, acceptance.

mcq.q: The two main approaches of black-box testing are:
o: Basis path testing and loop testing
Equivalence class partitioning and boundary value analysis
mcq.e: Basis path and loop testing are white-box methods.

mcq.q: For a program valid for the range 1 to 4000, boundary value analysis picks which test values?
mcq.e: BVA picks the edges and just-outside values: 0, 1, 4000, 4001.

mcq.q: Testing done at the customer's site in the real environment, with the developer absent, is:
mcq.e: Alpha testing happens at the developer's site in a controlled way.

mcq.q: Which testing deliberately plants small faults in code to check whether the test suite catches them?
mcq.e: Mutation testing is fault-based; if tests miss the planted faults, the suite is weak.

mcq.q: Which testing forces the software to fail in various ways and verifies that recovery is performed properly?
mcq.e: Regression testing instead re-runs old tests after a change.

mcq.q: Which integration testing approach is NOT incremental?
mcq.e: Big-bang combines all modules at once and tests the complete system in one go.

mcq.q: Which is NOT an accepted software quality factor?
mcq.e: Visibility describes the process, not the product quality factors; accepted factors include functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability and portability.

mcq.q: Which maintenance type involves adjusting software to a new operating system or hardware?
mcq.e: Corrective fixes faults, perfective improves performance, preventive restructures to avoid future problems.

mcq.q: In CMM, which level represents a documented, standardised process?
mcq.e: Level 3 is Defined; Level 4 Managed means the process is measured quantitatively.

mcq.q: Which statement about Gantt and PERT charts is correct?
o: A PERT chart can be derived from a Gantt chart
A Gantt chart can be derived from a PERT chart
Neither can be derived from the other
A Gantt chart contains task dependencies
mcq.e: A Gantt chart has no dependency information, so PERT cannot be derived from it.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a methodology for handling a risk?
mcq.e: Risks are handled by acceptance, avoidance or transfer.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a decomposition method of estimation?
o: Both LOC and FP are decomposition
mcq.e: COCOMO is an empirical formula-based model, not a decomposition method.

mcq.q: The COCOMO equation E = 3.2 x (KLOC)^1.05 corresponds to which mode of project?
mcq.e: Organic mode covers small, well-understood projects with small experienced teams.

mcq.q: A system has MTTF of 90 hours and MTTR of 10 hours. What is its MTBF?
mcq.e: MTBF = MTTF + MTTR = 90 + 10 = 100 hours.

mcq.q: Which of the following is a direct software measure?
mcq.e: Direct measures are LOC, cost, effort, speed and memory size; functionality, quality, efficiency and reliability are indirect.

mcq.q: Which attribute is NOT part of FURPS?
mcq.e: Portability enters only in FURPS+.

mcq.q: Which is NOT an attribute of good information?
mcq.e: The attributes are accuracy, timeliness, relevancy and completeness.

mcq.q: Strategic information is used for:
o: Long-term policy decisions by top management
mcq.e: Tactical information is medium-term and operational information is day-to-day.

mcq.q: Which information system records, validates, processes and stores day-to-day business transactions?
mcq.e: TPS is the base level system for day-to-day transactions.

mcq.q: Which are the resources of an MIS?
o: Hardware, software, education procedures and data
mcq.e: All four of hardware, software, people and data are MIS resources; 'education procedures' is not a component.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a prerequisite of a good MIS?
mcq.e: Prerequisites are database, qualified executives, control and maintenance, and top management support.

mcq.q: Knowledge that is highly personal, gained by experience and hard to formalise is called:
mcq.e: Explicit knowledge is documented and easily shared.

mcq.q: In an expert system, which component applies logical rules to derive conclusions?
mcq.e: The knowledge base holds what is known; the intelligent editor lets the domain expert enter knowledge.

mcq.q: OLX, where individuals sell to individuals, is an example of:
mcq.e: Consumer-to-consumer e-commerce connects individuals directly.

mcq.q: Packing, loading and shipping of goods belong to which step of the e-commerce process?
mcq.e: The primary process runs enquiry, offer, contract, delivery/fulfilment, billing, service.

mcq.q: Who is called the father of e-commerce in India?
mcq.e: K. Vaitheeswaran, founder of Fabmart/Indiaplaza, is given this title.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of electronic payment system?
mcq.e: EPS types include smart cards, e-wallets and EFT; a Demat account is used in online trading.

tf.s: Reverse engineering rebuilds an old system in a new form.
tf.n: Reverse engineering only understands the system; re-engineering rebuilds it.

tf.s: The Waterfall model is compatible with changing requirements.
tf.n: Any linear model is incompatible with changing requirements because requirements are frozen first.

tf.s: The Spiral model gives explicit recognition of risk on every cycle.
tf.n: Risk management is its most important feature.

tf.s: A DFD is also called a bubble chart because its processes are drawn as circles.
An SRS may include algorithms describing internal working of the system.
tf.n: The SRS is a black-box specification; algorithms belong to design.

tf.s: Low coupling and high cohesion is the golden rule of design.
tf.n: Loosely coupled, highly cohesive modules are the easiest to understand and maintain.

tf.s: Coincidental cohesion is the best type of cohesion.
tf.n: Coincidental is the worst; functional cohesion is the best.

tf.s: Validation asks 'Are we building the right product?'
tf.n: Validation checks the product against the user's actual need.

tf.s: White-box testing is also called glass-box testing.
tf.n: It tests the internal logic and code structure.

tf.s: Alpha testing is done at the customer's site with the developer absent.
tf.n: Alpha testing is at the developer's site; beta testing is at the customer's site.

tf.s: ISO 9000 certifies the software product rather than the process.
tf.n: ISO 9000 certifies the process, not the product.

tf.s: A PERT chart can be derived from a Gantt chart.
tf.n: A Gantt chart can be derived from a PERT chart, not the reverse, since Gantt lacks dependency information.

tf.s: Function points allow software size to be estimated before any code exists.
tf.n: FP measures size from functionality and is language-independent.
Mean Time Between Failures = Mean Time To Failure + Mean Time To Repair.

tf.s: Prototyping is a recognised software estimation technique.
tf.n: The recognised families are empirical, heuristic and analytical techniques.

tf.s: Delivery of an ordered item in e-commerce depends on its cost.
tf.n: Delivery depends on size, urgency and nature of the item, not on its cost.

fill.q: The SDLC phase that always comes immediately before Design is ______.
The Waterfall model is also called the ______ sequential model.
The Level-0 DFD, drawing the whole system as a single bubble, is called the ______ diagram.
In software design, the ______ type of coupling occurs when one module uses the code or data inside another and is the worst form.
The testing technique in which the programmer writes test scripts first and then code to pass them is called ______ (abbreviation).
The CMM level in which the process is measured quantitatively is called ______.
The four types of software maintenance are corrective, adaptive, perfective and ______.
The Gantt chart is prepared in the ______ phase of a project.
ROCOF stands for Rate of Occurrence of ______.
In e-commerce, a transplanted real-world business model that brings 'try before you buy' online is the ______ model.
